title: UseVisit Change Impact in Patient Chart

answers.question: If `useVisit` in the OpenMRS frontend framework (openmrs-esm-core) changed its behaviour, which code in the patient chart app (openmrs-esm-patient-chart) uses it and could be affected?

paragraphs.text: `useVisit` is the React hook the OpenMRS frontend framework uses to answer "does this patient have an open (active) visit right now?" — a visit being a period of care at a facility. It lives in `openmrs-esm-core` [1] and is re-exported to apps through `@openmrs/esm-framework` packages. The patient chart app (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart`) has a moderate number of real call sites (7 components) plus a much larger, hidden coupling: its cache-invalidation helpers hard-code the URL shape that `useVisit` uses as its SWR cache key.
## What the hook returns and how it fetches
`useVisit` returns seven things [2]: `activeVisit`, `currentVisit`, `currentVisitIsRetrospective`, `isLoading`, `isValidating`, `error` and `mutate`. It makes two SWR requests [3]:

- the active visit, fetched from `/visit?patient=<uuid>&v=<representation>&includeInactive=false` [4], then filtered client-side to the visit whose `stopDatetime === null` [5];
- the retrospective visit (a visit selected in the past), fetched by UUID [6].

It also writes into a shared store, `useVisitContextStore` [7], setting the visit context automatically when an active visit appears [8]. So a behaviour change here can move not just what components see but what the whole chart treats as the current visit.
Direct call sites, and the exact value each one depends on:

| Component | What it reads | Effect if behaviour changes |
|---|---|---|
| `VisitTag` banner tag [9] | `activeVisit`, `isLoading` | The blue "Active Visit" tag in the patient banner disappears or shows on the wrong patient |
| `VisitAttributeTags` [10] | `activeVisit` (`.attributes`) | Visit attribute tags vanish; `attributes` must be in the representation |
| `StopVisitOverflowMenuItem` [11] | `activeVisit` | The "End active visit" menu item is shown or hidden wrongly |
| `DeleteVisitOverflowMenuItem` [12] | `activeVisit` | "Delete active visit" appears wrongly, and `activeVisit` is passed to the dialog [13] |
| `EndVisitDialog` [14] | `activeVisit`, `mutate` | Ending a visit calls the hook's `mutate()` to refresh [15]; if `mutate` no longer refreshes both requests, the UI keeps showing an ended visit |
| `usePatientChartPatientAndVisit` [16] | `activeVisit`, `isValidating`, `mutate` | The most important one: this bootstraps the visit context and launches the patient-chart workspace group [17]. A change to `isValidating` or to when `activeVisit` becomes non-null alters which workspaces open. Note it deliberately calls `useVisit(null)` when a stored visit context exists [18], so a change to the null-guard at [19] hits this path |
| `VisitForm` [20] | `mutate` only | The form forwards `mutateVisitContext: mutateActiveVisit` into the workspace group props [21]; other components call it to refresh |
| `ExportedVisitForm` [22] | `activeVisit`, `isLoading` | Drives the overlapping-visit conflict check: `hasActiveVisitConflict` blocks saving when `activeVisit` is truthy and overlapping visits are off [23]. A wrong `activeVisit` here can block or wrongly allow new visits |
## The hidden coupling: cache keys and tests
Two things depend on `useVisit`'s internals rather than its return value:

1. **Cache-key string matching.** `invalidateVisitHistory` and `invalidateCurrentVisit` identify the hook's cache entry by matching the literal key `"{restBaseUrl}/visit?patient=<uuid>"` plus the flag `includeInactive=false` [24] and [25]. If `useVisit` changes its query parameters or URL order, `invalidateCurrentVisit` silently stops refreshing it. These helpers are called from many places, e.g. the visit form [26], `useDeleteVisit` [27], the mark-deceased workspace [28] and the order basket [29]. The comment at [30] states the intent explicitly: it targets history keys so it can avoid revalidating "the 28+ components that use current visit data via the useVisit hook", naming this pattern as a known performance concern.
   `useOptimisticVisitMutations` [31] and its `revalidateCurrentVisit`/`revalidateAllVisitData` [32] do the same, writing keys like `/visit?patient=<uuid>&v=custom` — note this omits `includeInactive=false`, so a hook-URL change would desynchronise optimistic updates from the hook's cache.

2. **The mock.** `mock.tsx` in the framework exports a stubbed `useVisit` returning `{ error: null, mutate, isValidating: true, currentVisit: null, activeVisit: null, currentVisitIsRetrospective: false }` [33], mirrored in `mock-jest.tsx`. Every test that mocks the hook must match its return shape; adding, renaming or removing a returned field breaks tests such as [34] and the eight `mockReturnValue` calls in [35]. Tests affected: `patient-chart.resources.test.ts`, `visit-tag.test.tsx`, `stop-visit.test.tsx`, `delete-visit.test.tsx`, `end-visit-dialog.test.tsx`, `visit-attribute-tags.test.tsx`, `visit-form.test.tsx`, plus `vitals-header.test.tsx` and `immunizations-detailed-summary.test.tsx` which import the hook without a local mock.

I read the patient chart at its default branch only; I did not check other branches or whether other selected repositories (e.g. the dispensing or laboratory apps) also call `useVisit`, since the question scoped it to the patient chart. I read the real call sites and the caching helpers, but I did not open every one of the 47 grep hits — the remaining hits are all test files already covered above. The `visited`/`useVisitContextStore` internals [7] are referenced by name only, so a change inside that store is a further path I have not traced.
